Subject: Integration & Dedicated capacity follow-up — NovaPay

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

TL;DR (read if you're short on time)
- NovaPay wants predictable inference costs and sub-200ms tail latency for payment routing suggestions at peak.
- Next step: 45-min technical deep-dive with your infra/security + Redwood SE to lock sizing and auth approach.

Notes from the call:
- Workload: ~1.2k peak QPS (burst to 2k during promos), avg tokens/request ~120, expected RLHF prompts for personalization.
- PII/security: data must remain in NovaPay VPC for production decisions; SOC2 evidence and KMS integration required.
- Integration surface: SDK + REST for sync requests, streaming for longer responses, structured JSON outputs for tool-calling (fraud-check and ledger microservice).
- Model plan: embed + reranker to shortlist candidates, then generator for final structured payload.
- SLA: target 95th percentile <200ms for inference path (we discussed baseline then caching/batching).

Open items / questions we need from your side before the deep-dive:
1) Confirm expected sustained QPS vs peak burst distribution across the day (sample hour-by-hour or 95/50/5 percentiles).
2) Provide a short list of typical prompts / example payloads we can use for evals (can be anonymized).
3) Security contacts and whether mTLS is required for SDK auth or standard API key + mutual TLS for provisioning.
4) Any blacklist/whitelist IP constraints for dedicated VPC peering.

Proposed next steps:
- Attach: mutual-action-plan-draft.docx (MPA draft) and a sizing template. Please review.
- We’ll schedule a technical deep-dive this week with Rishi and your infra lead (Alan). Can you share 3 available windows?
- Rishi will follow up with a preliminary Dedicated capacity estimate based on the numbers you just gave.

If okay, Rishi and I can prepare a short Dedicated-capacity proposal and a POC outline (2-week trial on a reserved pool) to run on anonymized traffic.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

Claire — thanks for the distribution. Quick notes from the SDK and integration standpoint: 

Authentication
- We support API key + optional mTLS for the Dedicated control plane. For Private deployments we typically enforce customer-managed KMS and mTLS for all node-to-node and control-plane communication.
- For short-lived credentials and least-privilege the SDK can request scoped tokens from your identity provider; we can wire a short demo for that.

Routing & Fallbacks
- Routing policy we recommend: region-preference -> model-cost tier -> fallback model variant (quantized smaller model) on saturation.
- For your latency targets, we'll configure headroom with a dedicated pool (min nodes) and burst autoscaling (max nodes) with a fast scale-up policy for short spikes.

Structured output + tool-calling
- SDK supports structured JSON outputs and our tool-calling hooks (signed webhook invocation). We can evolve the schema in the deep-dive and ship an example contract for your ledger microservice.

Next: Rishi and I will propose specific Dedicated sizing and a short POC runbook. See attached: redwood-sdk-auth-options.md (brief doc on auth flows).

I'll follow up with calendar options.

—Marissa

Subject: Dedicated capacity preliminary sizing & queueing notes — NovaPay

Claire / team — following the QPS doc and the call notes, initial Dedicated sizing and queueing recommendations below. This is a starting point for the technical deep-dive.

Assumptions (from data provided)
- 95th p95 QPS: 1,200 qps; bursts to 2,000 qps for ~10–15 minutes.
- Avg tokens per request: 120 tokens; 1 token ~ 1ms on the target GPU profile (this is conservative; we'll validate on benchmark).
- Target p95 latency: <200ms end-to-end for generator path (reranker target p95 <80ms).

Sizing suggestion (Dedicated GPU pool)
- Baseline pool: 6 x A100-equivalent instances (prediction: ~720 concurrent generations, depends on batch config).
- Burst capacity: allow autoscale up to 12 instances for promos (policy: scale on 1-min CPU/GPU utilization + queue depth).
- Concurrency limits: cap per replica at 120 concurrent request contexts; per-model concurrency configurable.
- Queueing: implement weighted priority queues — routing requests to a hot-path pool (low-latency users) vs background batch pool (non-critical).

Autoscaling policy (suggested)
- Warm pool: maintain min nodes = 6 to meet baseline.
- Scale up: aggressive scale when queue depth > 30 for 2 consecutive 30s windows.
- Scale down: gentle cooldown (10m) after sustained low utilization.

Caching & KV
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context (user profile snippets) to shave ~20–40ms for repeated users.

Embedding & reranker architecture
- Build embedding index in managed vector DB (we suggest approximate NN store). Reranker runs on same Dedicated pool but can be served as a separate, smaller model family pinned to lower latency nodes. If you need strict isolation, reranker can run on CPU-based infra but expect higher latency.

POC proposal
- 2-week POC on a reduced traffic slice: provision 2–3 replica pool with traffic mirroring for replay tests + canary to confirm latency & correctness.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.xlsx (workbook with baseline numbers and cost ranges).

I'll bring concrete per-GPU throughput numbers and a sample autoscaling policy to the tech deep-dive.

—Rishi

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful. A couple more questions before the tech sync: 

1) Cost estimate ballpark: can you give us a monthly commit estimate for the baseline and for the burst-capacity (high-level range is fine).
2) Tool-calling: our fraud microservice needs to be invoked with signed structured JSON and a synchronous OK/FAIL response. Will Redwood's tool-calling support HMAC-signed webhooks and retries?
3) Data residency / GDPR: we need confirmation that logs/audit traces for NovaPay production traffic remain in us regions only.
4) Timeline: if we sign a Reserved capacity agreement, how long to provision the Dedicated pool (VPC peering + onboarding)?

Alan — do you have bandwidth Wed 17:00 PST or Thu 09:00 PST for the sync?
